I,xceszsys.—A parliamentary return issued on ' li'edorsdav shows that in the year ended September 30,1879. licenses w.ere issued in the whole of the united Kingdom to 2,648 common brewers, not being victuallers or retail beer- millers; to 99,013 victuallers, to 37,849 persons to sell beer to be drunk on the premises, and to 10,079 persons to sell ' beer to he drunk off the premises. Of these, 2510 common brewers' licenses,69,B7o victuallers',, end the whole of the beersellers' license, were issued in England. 13,172 victual- lers, of whom 13,081 were in England, 90 in Scotland, and only one in Ireland, brewed their own lone, as did 6,558 retail twersellcre, all of whom were in England. The com- mon brewers consumed 46,650,637 bushels of malt, the victuallers 5,595,774 bushels, and the retail beersellern 2,824,375 bushels. PII2IIOOS WI(PLETAN Manful:awe SUIPDAT Ecnoot..— The seventieth annual Sunday school sertnona were preached in the Wesleyan Chapel, liccleston-street, Prescot, on Sun- day last, by thr Rev. J. Pollitt, of Colne, who preached ex- cellent sermons morning and evening, and delivered an ap- propriate address to the teachers and scholars in the alter- or. At each service a selection of hymns were sung by the children in a very pleasing manner. The attendance was all that could he desired ; in the evening the building was crowded. A collection was made at the close of each s. mice, and the amount realised was £l6. PEINCS Aanarn CAre, LIVERPOOL. Ross, Sr. HALT—vs.

I—The1—The mond of a series r.:f temperance enter:tainments was held in the above place on Saturday evening last, the choir being taken at eight pm. by Mr. J. Bridge, when an excel- lent programme of songs, recitations, bc.,was very creditably gone through. and seemed, judging by the plaudits and encores, to be thoroughly appreciated by the audience. Great credit is due to the manager of these rooms for his untiring efforts to institute in place of the I ste loose and Imp-hazard style of singing, boo really good moral enter- tainment, where a person can, at a very nominal charge, slip non Saturday evening and spend an hour with undeniable pleasore and profit. The promoters of this per Circler line of temperance work will, we trust, receive that encouragement end enemas which they so well deserve. div.head: ATTACKING A-MAN Willi A RATCHET.
div.p: ATTACKING A-MAN Willi A RATCHET.

- • At the Occasional Court House, Bank-street, Warrington, yesterday, a farm I.tbourer, named Martin Hoban, was charged, before Peter Stubs, Esq., with havlng unlawfully ' wounded Thomas Doffey with a hatchet, at Appleton, on the 10th March, 1879. The prisoner absconded after the occurrence, and was only apprehended yesterday. The prosecutor said he was now a tanner's tabourer, and lived in Latchford. On lite 10th March, 1879, he was work- ing as labourer for Mr. Petcival, a farmer, at Appleton. The prisoner, who was employed at the same place was dis- charged on that day, and he (witness) took his place. About half-past tive in the evening he went to the granary to make a tire when he found the prisoner there. He had a hatchet in his hand chopping firewood. He said to the prisoner thought you had gone away," but he replied No, I have not gone." Ile then said "You have no business here," when be replied he WAS there before witness, and would on there after hitn. l'risoner said he could not shift him, and he (witness) said he would get some one todo so. Prisoner then raised the hatchet up in his hands and began singing around wßness. He then stro k him on the bead with the edge of the hatchet and knocked him about three yards ender the heti. He endeavoured to rise, but could not do ao, and fell against a bed at the other side of the room. The blood blinded hitn, and he could [tot aee prisoner, but he begged of the prisoner not to kill him. He put his hand up to catch the prisoner, when the hatchet came into it, and as the prisoner could not release it he kicked witness in the ribs and ran away. With difficulty he found the door and went down the stairs, the blood still blinding him, but when he got within three steps of the bottom he fell. He wan seen by the servant girl, and taken into the house, where his wound was bathed. ele walked to the Stockton Heath Police Station, and I'S. 000th told him toga home and to even doctor. He walked home end then went to the Infim rary, o ~ tie. ber Richmond dreseed his wound. He was away from work a work, but when he went back ths nurse told hint he MAR not lit to work.—ln reply to the pri- soner, witness maid prisoner did not tell him he had corer for his "bits of things." Ile did not go to prisoner with a form in his hands and say be would have his life before he wem.

-1;r: Richmond said on the 10th of March, towards even- ing, the prosecutor came to the Infirmary with his wife. He was suffering from an incised wound about 2 inchea long, extending from the top of the forehead above the left eye to shout an inch above the right eyebrow. The edger of the wound were contused, and indicated that it might have been caused by 54DIC blunt-cutting instrument like an axe. The wound was not directly dangerous. ' P.S. Booth ItepOtled to directing the prosecutor to go to a tloctor with his wound on the 10th March, 1870, end on Friday maiming remiving the prisoner into custody from the Wa7ington police. . .
The prison'er had nothing to say, end w. committed for trial at the neat Quarter Sessions at Knuteford.

A statutory tneeting of the owners and ratepayers of the borough of Wdrrington waa convened in the Commercial Chamber of the Town Hall on Wednesday laat, at 12 o'clock at noon, for the purpose of passing a resolution, approving and consenting to the resolution passed by the Town Council on Tumdov, the 4th of May, to oppose in Perlis. ment a Bill for enabling the Corporation of Liverpool to obtain a supply of water from the rivers Vyrnwy, March- fleet, and Afon Conwy, in Montgomeryshire, and for other putposes: and that the Town Clerk be instructed to take sit the necessary steps by petition or otherwise, as may be deemed expedient for the due protection of the right, and interees of the borough of Warrington, as represented by the Council ; and that the costs, charges. and expenses I incdrred. and to be incurred, in such opposition, be charged upon the Borough Fund, Borough Rates, or other fund, or rate, oraccount of the said Council applicable thereto. There were presnt—lhe Mayor (J. R. Pickmere. Esq.), Aldermen Holmes Webster, and Burgess; Councillors Fairclough, Litton, Monks, Pollitt, Whittle, and Woods ; Brook (town der), and Chorley (borough treasurer.) Mr. Carson, a rate- payer, wee also present. The ltiAVOlt said it WAS scarcely necessary to say much as he hail Already expressed himself fully on the matter at the previous meeting of the Council. The subject upon which they had met had been well discussed, and the public were well aware of wlmt the Council desired by opposing the Liverpool Water Scheme. The main object they had in view was to prevent the Liverpool Corporation from lay- , log water Mid. In the bed of the river Mersey, as they were of °maim, it might impede the navigation of the river, and it was deeirable that the maMs ahould be laid some instance Below the bed. Another object they hat in view was the I obtaining of clansen in the Bill so that Vl'arrington, if de. sired, might be supplied with an adequate quantity of Imre water from the same source. He h:ol ph.asure in proparng the confirmation of the resolution passed on the 4th sp of May.

—Alderman Ifokstks .conded the motion. He said they , were aware that the water eupplied by the Warrington Waterworks Committee was certainly of an infg ior quality, and he thought if, by the insertion of certain clauses in the bill, they could be enabled at any thne to procure a supply of good water it would be a benefit to the town. He nbserved tint there was only one ratepayer present besides the reporters, and he suppoeed he shout I he in order in second- ing the resolution. Mr. Caesar expressed his pleasure at supporting the resolution. He fully agreed with Alderman Holmes Re to the water of the town,and it was aloo expedient that nothing should he done to impede the n.ay.igatiou or the river.
The resolution RAS then curried unanimously. The meeting then terminated.
